title: The Lurking Fear by H. P. Lovecraft

cognitive_validation.rationale: The story supplies a systematic, nonsupernatural, immanent account: degeneration down the evolutionary scale from ancestry, isolation, intermarriage and cannibalism; heritable Martense mismatched eyes tracing lineage; and an investigative method (tabulation of incidents, deduction of the radiating tunnel network) that explains the phenomenon as a living organism, not a ghost. The pseudo-scientific logic of hereditary and evolutionary regression suffices as imaginary science even without present-day accuracy.

novum_candidates.description: The lurking fear is revealed as a swarm of thousands of degenerated, semi-subterranean, cannibalistic subhuman creatures\u2014the devolved descendants of the isolated, inbreeding Martense family\u2014who have honeycombed Tempest Mountain with tunnels and emerge during thunderstorms to kill. This candidate is a coherent pseudo-biological novum: multi-generational evolutionary regression driven by isolation, inbreeding, and cannibal nutrition, producing a hidden branching of humanity into a monstrous species.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The reader-facing contrast is explicit: after the revelation one cannot think of the earth's unknown caverns without nightmare dread, transferring the horror onto ordinary wells and subways. Storyworld consequences include the mass destruction of the mansion and mountaintop and the extrapolation that analogous degenerate phenomena may exist worldwide. Character reactions (marvel at surviving sane, chronic trauma requiring opiates, fear of being called mad) are recorded separately as estrangement evidence and are not required for qualification.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The degenerate Martense creatures govern the whole narrative: the village massacre, the entire investigation, the deaths of companions, the underground crawl, the climactic swarm, and the final dynamiting of the mountain all follow from and resolve upon this novum. It is the overriding narrative logic rather than an incidental device.

novelty.rationale: The revelation that an entire human family has degenerated into thousands of subterranean cannibal ape-things constitutes a totalizing difference from the empirical norm: the narrator explicitly extrapolates that such hidden degenerate phenomena may exist worldwide and that the earth's caverns now carry nightmare implications, altering the storyworld's understanding of humanity and the underground.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The investigators hypothesize a living organism highly susceptible to electrical storms, giving a partial systematic account, but the mechanism linking thunder to emergence is asserted rather than explained.

novum_candidates.description: The creatures' behavioral coupling to thunderstorms\u2014the notion that lightning/thunder 'calls' the lurking fear from its underground lair to hunt\u2014as a distinct environmental-biological trait of the phenomenon.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The only lingering estrangement tied specifically to storms is the narrator's need for opiates when it thunders; this is recorded as character reaction rather than as a qualifying dimension.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The storm-coupling is a recurring motif and trigger but does not itself determine the overriding narrative logic; the driving explanation and resolution rest on the Martense degeneration. It is an incidental trait subordinate to the dominant novum.

novelty.rationale: Susceptibility to electrical storms is an unusual trait, but it functions as an attribute of the broader degeneration novum rather than a separate world-altering difference. On its own it does not totalize a distinct story universe.
